text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in cross-region 5xx + DNS SERVFAILs observed for eu->us egress paths (eu-west2 -> us-west1). 5xx rate up 12x over baseline. Paging on-call. See runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/cross-region-routing

sre_jordan: on it. pinging netops, gathering impact numbers. can someone confirm if this is only egress from eu-west2 or also other AZs?

eng_oncall_mina: I see increased latency and SERVFAILs from probes to us-west1-edge from two eu-west2 AZs (a, b). Dumping edge logs now.

infra_rajeev: looking at route-manager, noticed a flurry of policy changes around 12:02Z — a promo job touched region-pinning for a subset of prefixes. rolling back to previous policy now.

netops_li: confirmed — BGP communities for a few prefixes got tagged for cross-region preference by the promo. rolling community unset to restore local egress.

eng_oncall_mina: ACLs and health-checks ok. DNS query logs show increased NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL from our upstream resolvers towards vendor-resolver-2.us-west1. Possibly overloaded or responding with SERVFAIL when cross-region pinned.

infra_rajeev: rollback applied to routing policy. pushing a temporary pin-disable override: `route-manager set --policy region-pin --state disabled --scope eu-west2 --ttl 300`

eng_oncall_mina: applied override. watching. Metrics: cross-region 5xx rate down from 12x -> 3x in 40s, latency 95p dropping.

product_olivia: any customer-facing impact? do we need to open a status page incident?

customer_ops_tom: support queue shows 6 customers reporting increased error rates for embeddings and chat calls originating EU. All mapped to eu-west2. Recommend posting status page with 'partial service disruption' for EU->US routing.

sre_jordan: agreed. I'll open INC-2026-472 and post an interim message: "Partial disruption: some EU requests to US models may fail or slow. Mitigation underway."

netops_li: vendor-resolver-2 support reached out — they are seeing high query amplification tied to unexpected EDNS behavior with cross-region TTLs. We're coordinating a filter fix on their side.

eng_oncall_mina: temporary mitigation: increasing local resolver TTL usage and enabling aggressive client-side caching for prefix X via `dns-config --local-cache 60s` to reduce upstream QPS. Doing now.

infra_rajeev: also enabling a soft-failover in routing: `route-manager set --policy latency-fallback --enable --threshold 250ms` so requests exceeding latency fallback to nearest replica.

eng_oncall_mina: after these steps, 5xx back to ~1.1x baseline and latency near normal. Customer reports decreasing.

product_olivia: good. keep status updated. we should plan a postmortem and notify affected customers with timeline.

sre_jordan: taking incident lead. short-term actions recorded in the runbook. Postmortem owner: @sre_shift_next_sam. ETA for handoff: 02:00Z.

customer_ops_tom: noted. I'll prepare a customer bulletin draft and include what to expect and remediation steps.

netops_li: vendor will roll a resolver patch in ~45m. keeping pin-disable until we confirm stability for 2 hours.

eng_oncall_mina: handoff to next on-call in 25m. leaving watch on metrics and alert thresholds lowered to catch regression.

sre_shift_next_sam: taking postmortem owner. will verify routing policy audit logs, DNS QPS patterns, and the promo job that caused initial policy change.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT UPDATE recorded (INC-2026-472). Current status: mitigated -> monitoring. Escalation: vendor resolver patch pending.

sre_jordan: closing paging loop for primary on-call. if anything spikes, ping this thread and escalate to pager. great teamwork. :thumbsup:
